chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
It was among what Musa (Moses) confided to his Lord, that he said: O Lord! What reward is reached by visiting the sick?
So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: I will appoint an angel with him, visiting him in his grave until his resurrection.

key_terms.أَجْر: Ajr — reward from God, especially in the afterlife context
key_terms.عِيَادَة: 'Iyada — the act of visiting the sick; a highly recommended Sunnah with specific etiquette
key_terms.مَحْشَر: Mahshar — the place and time of gathering on the Day of Resurrection
key_terms.نَاجَى: Munajat — intimate, secret supplication or conversation with God; used especially of prophets' private communion with God

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the sick according to a hadith about Moses asking God?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) narrates a divine conversation in which the Prophet Musa (Moses) asked his Lord about the reward for visiting the sick. God responded that He will assign an angel to accompany the visitor in his grave until the Day of Resurrection, providing perpetual companionship and intercession in the barzakh. This hadith was transmitted in the context of al-Kulayni's chapter on the spiritual rewards of 'iyada (sick visitation), emphasizing that acts of compassion toward the ill carry extraordinary eschatological consequences.
